Splitting text lines and inline shader reveal

I saw Yousuf Soomro's Slot Field and Manoela Ilic's Inline Hover Reveals and wanted to know if one live HTML essay inside an ElementGL canvas can slide neighbouring lines apart vertically on the GPU without reflowing the DOM. Hover, tap or select an anchor word, edit the inline phrase, or switch between pixel blocks and the optical GLSL ribbon.

Slot field essay · 4 anchors · 0 DOM reflow rest · click or hover

When Chrome draws DOM into a texture, every glyph stays crisp inside one live element. I slice that picture along the anchor line bounds so surrounding prose parts vertically while refraction or pixel noise opens behind the chosen word.

Keeping honest takes a second step because WebGL texture uploads leave Chromium's click boxes at rest. Here the anchored line stays unshifted while neighbouring strips glide outward, and glyphs across the opened slot stay readable and selectable.

Type inside this editable inline phrase to trigger a fresh paint event and watch the cached Range line rectangles update without layout shift.

Show the code cached Range line slicing, 3-strip WebGL shader, hit mapping and 2D 9-arg fallback
  1. One live essay inside the canvas. Semantic paragraphs with inline <button> and <a> anchors, a contenteditable span and a Pin slot toggle sit inside a single drawable article.
  2. Cached line slicing with Range.getClientRects(). Reads each anchor's box and full line band relative to #slot-article at resize or input time, so the animation loop never forces layout.
  3. Three-strip WebGL fragment shader. Shifts aboveAnchor up and belowAnchor down by gap / 2, keeps the chosen anchor word steady in place, and fills the cavity with 8 px pixel blocks or an optical GLSL ribbon.
  4. Geometry sync and inverse pointer mapping. Scales updateElementGeometry() by geometryUnit() with dataset.hitTick, and maps clicks on slid strips back to rest coordinates.
  5. Nine-argument 2D slice fallback. Cuts the same three horizontal bands with 9-argument drawElementImage() and restores the article's full hit region with an empty-clip 5-argument draw.

How it works

This page puts Yousuf Soomro's Slot Field (post) together with Manoela Ilic's Inline Hover Reveals (demo) on a single <canvas content="drawable" layoutsubtree>. Instead of cloning text into separate DOM spans and animating margins or transforms per line, the essay stays one plain <article drawable> inside the canvas.

  • Cached line measurement at rest: when the article mounts, resizes or receives input inside #editable-line, measureAnchors() creates a Range over each anchor's containing paragraph and reads getClientRects(). Merging all inline rects on the same vertical band gives [lineTop, lineBottom] around every ascender and descender without reading layout inside requestAnimationFrame().
  • Single ElementGL upload inside paint: the page waits for hasPainted === true inside the canvas paint listener before calling stage.upload(articleEl) (gl.texElementSubImage2D()). Active spring frames reuse that GPU texture and update uniforms only.
  • Three-strip split with zero DOM reflow: the canvas reserves 32 px of dark backing above and below the article sheet. As slotGap springs from 0 to 58 px, the fragment shader slides aboveAnchor up by gap / 2 and belowAnchor down by gap / 2, fades surrounding words on anchorLine into ghosted glyphs, and holds the active keyword crisp inside an illuminated capsule.
  • Two shader cavities: Mode 1 renders quantised 8 px animated pixel blocks and edge scan ticks inspired by Slot Field. Mode 2 renders an iridescent GLSL fluid and optical interference ribbon underneath the live link inspired by Inline Hover Reveals. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce (or the checkbox above), slotGap snaps in one frame and pixel flicker freezes.
  • Unshifted anchor hit-testing and shifted strip mapping: because anchorLine stays at dy = 0 px while outer strips part around it, keeping updateElementGeometry() at rest aligns the active <button> or <a> 1:1 with document.elementsFromPoint(). For clicks on slid strips, mapCanvasYToArticleY() inverts ±gap / 2 back to article layout coordinates so clicking another anchor or Pin slot still lands on the right target.
  • Nine-argument 2D and plain-HTML fallbacks: switching the Route control to 2D (9-arg slice) swaps in a fresh canvas, retires the WebGL canvas through window.__gfx.retire() and slices the same three strips using 9-argument drawElementImage(), ending with an empty-clip 5-argument draw so the hit box isn't shrunk to the last slice. If HTML-in-canvas isn't available or a context is lost, the essay moves into plain HTML without losing your edits.
